branch: origin/partial_redraw (mod source under Mods/Cartograph/Source/Cartograph; tip commit da80b33684 "WIP: Partial redraw", parent 2de05ef1dd / c678d0268a / a23189ba1d)
purpose: First attempt to implement issue #10 (localized/partial redraws). Predecessor of the current scissor-based partial redraw. It tries to avoid clearing+redrawing the entire 8192x8192 render target on every single build/remove event by (a) accumulating an FBox2D 'UpdateArea' covering only the changed buildings, (b) clearing only that rectangle, and (c) re-drawing only the buildings whose bounds overlap that rectangle, looked up via a quadtree. It also adds an event-driven incremental quadtree (Insert/Remove on add/remove) so the overlap query is cheap. The branch predates the GameFeature (1.2) refactor, the Z-height filter, layer categories, the index-redirector quadtree, and the client/server RCO transfer that exist on the current Cartograph branch.
approachSummary: Same high-level pipeline as the current branch (hook AddBuildable/RemoveBuildable + Lightweight subsystem Add/Invalidate -> push into PendingAdd/RemoveBuildingData -> coroutine RedrawMapCoroutine with a per-tick FTickTimeBudget). The DIFFERENCE is the clear+cull strategy. partial_redraw clears geometrically on the CPU: clear_render_target_portion() draws an OPAQUE BLACK FCanvasTileItem sized to exactly cover UpdateArea (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:67-79, called at :411-413 of the WIP), then queries CurrentBuildingQuadTree.GetElements(UpdateArea, BuildingsToRedraw) and redraws only those. The current Cartograph branch instead ALWAYS draws a FULL-SCREEN clear tile (CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:653-660) and a full-screen-sized draw, but clips both to the changed region with a GPU SCISSOR RECT computed from RedrawArea (ScissorArea at :633-651) and applied on the render thread via a custom FCartographCanvasRenderItem that calls RHICmdList.SetScissorRect (CartographCanvasRenderItem.cpp:102-115). Quadtree element type also differs: partial_redraw stores FBuildingData BY VALUE in TQuadTree<FBuildingData> (header:128) and Insert/Removes the actual struct (cpp:599-639); the current branch stores TQuadTree<int32> plus a BuildingDataIndexRedirector array to map quadtree ids back to CurrentBuildingData indices without re-balancing the tree on every shift (header:365-366, OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove :1194-1234). So: partial_redraw = CPU geometric clear + value-quadtree; current = GPU scissor clip + index-redirector-quadtree.
keyChanges: WIP diff da80b33684 adds FBox2D UpdateArea member (header:125) and accumulates it from GetBuildableBounds() of each added/removed building inside the FCancellationGuard block (cpp:368-372, 376-380)

Replaces the unconditional full-map clear_render_target_portion(...whole map...) with a branch: if IsInitializing -> clear whole map + draw CurrentBuildingData; else -> clear_render_target_portion(Canvas, UpdateArea) + CurrentBuildingQuadTree.GetElements(UpdateArea, BuildingsToRedraw) and draw only those (cpp:395-411 of WIP)

Incremental quadtree maintained event-driven in AddToCurrentBuildingData/RemoveFromCurrentBuildingData (cpp:599-639): Insert(BuildingData, *Bounds) / Remove(BuildingData, *Bounds). Commit 2de05ef1dd introduced this; commit c678d0268a introduced the partial clear tile

GetBuildableBounds (cpp:472-501) computes a 2D OBB from BuildableSize+Transform (or uses the cached actor-bounds BoundingBox for heavy AFGBuildable actors) and ExpandBy(1.5) — this is what feeds both the quadtree and UpdateArea

FBuildingData carries TWeakObjectPtr<AFGBuildable> Buildable + TOptional<FBox2D> BoundingBox + Transform + CustomizationData (header:25-33); splines/wires are redrawn by re-reading the live USplineComponent every redraw (cpp:421-470)
salvageableIdeas: The geometric (CPU) clear via an opaque black tile sized to UpdateArea is conceptually correct and is the cheapest possible clear — it touches only the dirty pixels and needs no custom render item / scissor plumbing. Worth keeping as a fallback / for platforms where the scissor hack is fragile.

Accumulating a single FBox2D UpdateArea across a batch of pending adds+removes (cpp:368-380) is the right granularity for batching many same-frame events into one redraw, and the current branch kept exactly this idea (RedrawArea). Confirms the batched-dirty-rect model is the intended design.

Event-driven incremental quadtree maintained on add/remove (cpp:599-639) instead of rebuilding per redraw is the key scalability win for large factories — the current branch adopted this (with the int-redirector twist). The overlap query CurrentBuildingQuadTree.GetElements(UpdateArea, ...) is what makes localized redraw O(overlap) instead of O(all buildings).

Caching the actor bounding box (BoundingBox / VisualBoxCache) at insert time so redraw never re-calls GetActorBounds is a real memory-vs-CPU tradeoff worth preserving; the current branch generalized it to VisualBoxCache.

Splitting InitializeTimeBudget vs RedrawTimeBudget (config) and co_await Budget per element to spread work across frames is the correct anti-lag-spike lever for issue #14 — directly addresses the 15s stalls if budgets are tuned low enough.
pitfalls: INCOMPLETE / UNTESTED by author's own admission: commit messages '2de05ef1dd ... NOT TESTED' and tip is literally 'WIP'. The TODO at cpp:417 ('TODO: Stencil subsequent draws to UpdateArea if not initializing') reveals the core unsolved problem: draws are NOT clipped to UpdateArea. So drawing a building whose bounds straddle UpdateArea will paint pixels OUTSIDE the cleared rectangle and corrupt neighbours, OR a redrawn neighbour can over-paint. The whole reason the current branch invented the FCartographCanvasRenderItem scissor was to fix exactly this gap — partial_redraw's clear and draw are not co-clipped.

FCanvasTileItem clear with SE_BLEND_Opaque writes alpha=0 black; because it's opaque it overwrites, but it is a DRAW (geometry) not a fast RHI clear — fine for small rects, but if UpdateArea grows huge (e.g. one belt spanning the map, or a remove of a foundation far from an add) the 'partial' clear degenerates toward full-map cost with none of the batching guards the current branch added.

Quadtree stores FBuildingData BY VALUE (TQuadTree<FBuildingData>): each element is a full struct (weakptr + TOptional<FBox2D> + FTransform(48B+) + FFactoryCustomizationData). For a multi-100k-building factory this roughly DOUBLES the per-building memory (one copy in CurrentBuildingData, one in the tree) — directly aggravates the known high-memory complaint. The current branch's TQuadTree<int32>+redirector exists specifically to avoid this duplication.

TQuadTree<FBuildingData>::Remove relies on FBuildingData::operator== which compares only BuildableClass + Transform.Equals (cpp:88-91). Two identical buildables at the same transform (or float-equal transforms) are indistinguishable -> Remove can delete the wrong element or fail, desyncing tree from CurrentBuildingData. The redirector approach in the current branch sidesteps identity-based removal.

Splines/wires are redrawn by dereferencing the LIVE USplineComponent during redraw and explicitly do NOT co_await inside the segment loop ('the Buildable ... might become invalid after resuming', cpp:457-459). On a partial redraw triggered by a far-away edit, a spline that merely OVERLAPS UpdateArea gets fully re-walked every time, and a since-removed spline's weakptr can be stale — a plausible contributor to the #14 crash and to redundant work. Spline geometry is never cached into the dirty-rect model.

UpdateArea is reset to {} at the end of a successful redraw (cpp:530 of WIP) but on CANCELLATION the added/removed lists are re-fed via OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled while UpdateArea handling lives inside the cancelled coroutine — the dirty rect can be lost or double-counted across cancel/restart, causing missed clears (ghost buildings) — a regression risk the current branch had to design around with IsPendingRedrawEntire.

Architecturally stale: no GameFeature module split, no Z-height filter, no layer categories, no client RCO initial-data transfer, no class-hash compaction (ClassIDToClassPtrMap). Cannot be merged forward; it is reference material only for the redraw algorithm, not a backport candidate.
recommendation: Do NOT revive or merge origin/partial_redraw — it is a self-described WIP that is architecturally two major refactors behind (pre-1.2, pre-GameFeature) and, critically, never solved the clip-the-draw problem (the cpp:417 'TODO: Stencil' is the unfinished half). The current Cartograph branch already supersedes it: it kept the good ideas (batched dirty-rect 'RedrawArea', event-driven quadtree, cached bounds, dual time budgets) and additionally solved the gap partial_redraw left open by co-clipping BOTH the clear and the redraw with a GPU scissor (FCartographCanvasRenderItem). For fixing memory/lag/crash, mine partial_redraw only for these confirmed-good directions and apply them on the current branch: (1) keep TQuadTree<int32>+redirector — partial_redraw's value-quadtree is a memory regression, not a fix; (2) the real remaining wins for issue #14/#10 are upstream of the redraw — cap/clamp RedrawArea growth so a single far-spanning edit can't escalate to a near-full redraw, cache spline polyline geometry into the dirty-rect model instead of re-walking live USplineComponents every redraw, and lower the per-tick RedrawTimeBudget to bound frame cost; (3) for the high-memory complaint, the actionable lever is shrinking per-building storage (the FBuildingData footprint and the 8192x8192 = 256MB+ RGBA render target), not anything partial_redraw offers. Net: treat partial_redraw as a historical design note confirming the dirty-rect approach, and concentrate fixes on RedrawArea-growth clamping, spline caching, budget tuning, and render-target/struct memory on the current branch.

branch: origin/Cartograph_2.0 (mod source under Mods/Cartograph/Source/Cartograph; older non-GameFeature layout)
purpose: An in-progress, never-finished rewrite ("Cartograph_2.0") that aims to replace the CPU FCanvas->RenderTarget drawing pipeline with a GPU SceneCapture2D approach: place every buildable as a real (but render-only) mesh/marker actor in the world, then use a UMapCaptureComponent2D (a USceneCaptureComponent2D subclass) to capture a top-down orthographic view into the map render target. The two newest commits (a54df0180e "Done some work needed for POC", 0ccd71d148 "Proof of concept implementation") are explicitly POC scaffolding; the branch is otherwise the same 1.x canvas codebase. Goal: get rendering off the game thread / off the CPU canvas so build/remove no longer trigger CPU redraw passes (issues #14 lag spikes, #10 full-redraw inefficiency).
approachSummary: Architecturally inverts the rendering model. CURRENT branch: data-driven CPU rasterization. Each buildable is converted to an FBuildingData record (CartographDataStructure.h) held in a sorted TArray CurrentBuildingData + a TQuadTree<int32> (CartographGameInstanceModule.h). On every build/remove event the RedrawMapCoroutine (CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:546-892) calls BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget on an 8192x8192 UCanvasRenderTarget2D, draws a full-screen opaque clear tile (line 653-660), then re-draws every visible building as FCanvasTileItem/draw_line, clipped by a scissor rect (CartographCanvasRenderItem). 2.0 branch: scene-graph + GPU capture. CartographGameWorldModule::DispatchLifecycleEvent (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:31-95) walks AFGBuildableSubsystem::GetAllBuildablesRef() and the lightweight-buildable subsystem once at world load, and for each buildable adds an instance (transform scaled to the buildable's bounding box) into a per-type instanced component on a single MapMarkerActor; splines/wires/beams become thin oriented box instances via get_line_transform. Then MapCapture->ShowOnlyActorComponents(MapMarkerActor) + CaptureSceneDeferred() renders the whole factory to the RT in one GPU pass. UMapCaptureComponent2D overrides GetViewOwner() so the capture's show-only/hide lists resolve per-owner. The redraw cost moves from O(buildings) CPU draw calls per event to a single GPU capture; per-building updates would become a cheap instance add + one re-capture instead of a canvas redraw.
keyChanges: New UMapCaptureComponent2D : USceneCaptureComponent2D (MapCaptureComponent2D.h/.cpp) overriding GetViewOwner() to return GetOwner() — standard UE trick to make per-capture ShowOnlyActors/HiddenActors and bOnlyOwnerSee filtering work so the map capture only sees the marker meshes, not the real world.

CartographGameWorldModule gains the entire new render path (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:31-330): MapMarkerActor + MapCapture members (GameWorldModule.h:62-67), AddBuildable(), GetNiagaraComponentPerType(), and GetBuildingBoundingBox().

GetBuildingBoundingBox (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:189-275) computes each buildable class's footprint from GetCombinedClearanceBox(), falling back to walking InheritableComponentHandler templates + SimpleConstructionScript nodes + native CDO subobjects, cached in a static BuildableBoundingBoxCache. This replaces the current branch's GetBuildingSize logic and is reusable regardless of render backend.

New FBuildableVisual / FLineVisual structs (fill color, border, opacity, thickness, mesh, materials) keyed per category / material / buildable (GameWorldModule.h:14-100) — a cleaner visual-config model than the current FCategoryData/FSplineData/FWireData triplet.

Content assets added: TwoPointO/ folder with RT_Map, M_Map, M_MapMarker, NS_MapMarker + NS_SplineMapMarker (Niagara systems), SM_Cube, BP_MapMarkerManager, Hook_Map_Cartograph — i.e. the design migrated from ISM toward Niagara mesh-renderer particles for the markers.

Spline/wire/beam handling: instead of CPU draw_line per segment, splines sample 8 points along the USplineComponent and emit oriented unit-cube instances scaled to segment length (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:148-170); wires/beams use get_line_transform.

CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp lost only the duplicate DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY (moved to CartographHelpers.cpp); the canvas RedrawMapCoroutine, CurrentBuildingData, QuadTree, and per-event RedrawMap(false) hooks all still exist unchanged in 2.0.
salvageableIdeas: The SceneCapture2D direction itself is the single biggest structural win: it offloads rasterization to the GPU and makes 'redraw' a fixed-cost capture rather than O(N) CPU FCanvasTileItem draws. This is the right tool to kill issue #14 lag spikes and issue #10's full-redraw cost — a capture of static instanced geometry costs roughly the same whether 1 or 100k buildings changed.

Instanced rendering (ISM/HISM or Niagara mesh renderer) for markers: adding/removing a buildable becomes AddInstance/RemoveInstance (O(1) amortized) on a per-type component, eliminating the need to keep a parallel FBuildingData TArray + scissor math + quad-tree-of-redraw-rects entirely. Incremental updates become trivial.

GetBuildingBoundingBox via GetCombinedClearanceBox() with CDO-walking fallback (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:189-275) is backend-agnostic and more robust than current size derivation; port it regardless of which render path wins.

Reading lightweight buildables directly from AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem::GetAllLightweightBuildableInstances() at init (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:42-90) is a cleaner bulk-gather than the current InitialBuildableGather coroutine and avoids per-instance actor overhead for belts/pipes (the exact class in issue #14's belt-triggered crash).
GetViewOwner() override is the minimal, correct mechanism to make the capture see ONLY the marker layer — keep it.

Per-buildable-class instance batching (NiagaraComponentPerType / one component per type) is the right granularity: it bounds component count to the number of buildable types (~hundreds), not instances (~100k+).
pitfalls: NOT FUNCTIONAL / DOES NOT COMPILE. CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:104-135 is broken: it declares `auto* Niagara = ...AddComponentByClass(UNiagaraComponent...)`, calls `Niagara->SetAsset()` with NO argument and NO semicolon, then operates on an undeclared `Ism` variable (leftover from an ISM->Niagara refactor) — GetNiagaraComponentPerType and AddBuildable reference `GetIsm()` which no longer exists. The Niagara module is still commented out in Cartograph.Build.cs:38 (`//"Niagara"`), so even the includes won't link. This is throwaway scaffolding, not a runnable branch.

Half-migrated dual architecture: CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp in 2.0 is virtually unchanged — it still contains the full canvas RedrawMapCoroutine (BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget at line 625), CurrentBuildingData, the QuadTree, and per-build-event RedrawMap(false) hooks (lines 137,168,197,229,259). The new path only runs once in GameWorldModule::DispatchLifecycleEvent at POST_INITIALIZATION. There is NO incremental add-on-build/remove-on-demolish wiring for the SceneCapture path, and no menu/z-filter/layer-toggle integration. Both systems would currently fight over the same RenderTarget.

The 8192x8192 RenderTarget is untouched and remains the dominant MEMORY cost: at RGBA8 that's ~268 MB GPU, and SceneCapture pipelines often need an additional same-size scene-color/HDR target + readback, which could WORSEN memory unless the format/resolution is reduced. The capture approach does nothing for the memory complaint by itself.

SceneCapture2D triggers a real render-thread scene render; if invoked synchronously per build event (CaptureScene rather than CaptureSceneDeferred, or capturing every frame) it can stall the render thread and re-introduce hitches/GPU TDR — the exact class of failure in issue #14. Capture cadence must be throttled/coalesced.

Capture correctness: ShowOnlyActorComponents only filters by actor; the marker actor's instances must be on a layer/owner the main player camera never renders, and the capture must use an orthographic projection sized exactly to the world bounds (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH constants) — none of that ortho setup is in the C++ (it lives in unread .uasset BP_MapMarkerManager/RootGameWorld assets), so it's unverifiable from source.

Multiplayer/dedicated-server story regresses: the current design serializes CurrentBuildingData to clients via the RemoteCallObject (CartographRemoteCallObject.cpp:48) and clients redraw locally. The 2.0 path gathers buildables directly from the subsystems on each instance, which can work client-side, but the existing RCO/ClientUpdateBuildingData replication and the server-only `FPlatformProperties::IsServerOnly() co_return` skip are not adapted — relevant to dedicated-server crash issue #9.

Memory leak risk in the new path: AddBuildable adds instances but MarkedBuildingIndices/NiagaraComponentPerType have no removal/cleanup code; demolishing buildings would orphan instances and grow unboundedly across a session.

Spline sampling is hardcoded to 8 segments and writes into a function-local `static TArray<FTransform>` (CartographGameWorldModule.cpp:148) — a static mutable shared across all calls; not thread-safe and a latent bug if capture ever moves off the game thread.
recommendation: Do NOT adopt origin/Cartograph_2.0 as-is and do not try to "finish" it by merging — it is a non-compiling proof-of-concept (broken Niagara/ISM code, Niagara module not linked, no incremental updates, no UI/filter integration, dual conflicting render paths) whose real design lives in unread .uasset blueprints, not in C++. Instead, treat it as a validated DIRECTION and re-implement on the current GameFeature branch in stages: (1) Quick wins on the existing canvas path first — they directly target the open issues without an architecture rewrite: drop RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE from 8192 to ~4096 (4x memory cut, ~268MB->~67MB) or use a lower-bpp/compressed RT format; ensure the per-event RedrawMap(false) coalesces (issue #10/#14) — the scissor/partial-redraw machinery and RedrawTimeBudget already exist (RedrawMapCoroutine), so verify build events are debounced into one capped redraw per frame rather than one coroutine per event. (2) Then prototype the SceneCapture2D path properly on a fresh branch: port GetBuildingBoundingBox and the lightweight-subsystem bulk gather, render markers via HISM (simpler/no Niagara dependency) on a hidden marker actor with UMapCaptureComponent2D + GetViewOwner override, set an orthographic projection matching the WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH bounds, and gate capture behind CaptureSceneDeferred throttled to at most once per N frames and only when the map is actually visible. Wire incremental AddInstance/RemoveInstance into the existing build/remove hooks and add instance cleanup on demolish (the missing piece in 2.0). Keep the FBuildingData/RCO replication only if the capture must run server-side; otherwise let each client gather locally. Salvage the bounding-box, instancing, and GetViewOwner ideas; discard the half-migrated CartographGameInstanceModule canvas coexistence and the broken Niagara code.

branch: origin/show_buildable_ui (5 commits ahead of merge-base 25a86bb0af "Bump version", 2025-03-24; pre-1.2-GameFeature, source under Mods/Cartograph/Source/Cartograph)
purpose: A UI-feature prototype, NOT a performance branch. Goal: let the user hover/click a building on the rendered map and pop up that building's native interaction widget (UFGInteractWidget) inside the map view. Adds a hover-area widget (BPW_HoverArea), a building-info container (BPW_BuildingUIContainer), an EnhancedInput "Cycle Building" action (key E / IMC_UI mapping context), and the screen->world picking that turns a map click into the building under the cursor. The last 2 commits ("Prevent inventory from opening", "Fiddling with inventory opening...") are an unfinished fight to stop FGGameUI from auto-opening the player inventory when the interact widget spawns.
approachSummary: Architecturally orthogonal to the current Cartograph branch's performance model — it reuses the existing render/data plumbing and bolts interaction on top, rather than changing how the map is drawn or stored. The one data-model change is additive and harmful for memory: it appends a per-building TSoftObjectPtr<AFGBuildable> BuildablePtr to FBuildingData (CartographDataStructure.h:93) so a map pixel can be resolved back to a live actor. The map-picking reuses the SAME spatial index the current branch already uses for partial redraw: OnCycleBuildings (CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:1383) does CurrentBuildingQuadTree.GetElements({World,World}, ...) then maps quadtree ids through BuildingDataIndexRedirector — identical pattern to the current branch's RedrawMapCoroutine query (origin/Cartograph CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:686-691). So it does not introduce a new/faster data structure; it consumes the existing one for a point query. It does NOT touch RedrawMap, the redraw budget, the full-vs-partial redraw decision, NetSerialize cost, or InitialBuildableGather. The branch was abandoned: the current Cartograph branch contains NONE of it (no OnCycleBuildings/CurrentBuildableUI/HoverArea/BuildablePtr — confirmed by grep over origin/Cartograph).
keyChanges: CartographDataStructure.h:93 — adds `TSoftObjectPtr<AFGBuildable> BuildablePtr` to FBuildingData; set in AddExtraData (CartographDataStructure.cpp:237). This grows EVERY building record and directly worsens the memory complaint (#14): TSoftObjectPtr embeds an FSoftObjectPath = 2x FName + an FString sub-path, ~48+ bytes plus heap-allocated string per building, times potentially 100k+ buildings.

CartographDataStructure.cpp NetSerialize — BuildablePtr is NOT serialized (only set in AddExtraData on the server/host path). So on dedicated-server clients receiving replicated FBuildingData, BuildablePtr is empty and the whole pick feature silently no-ops; the field is pure memory overhead there.

CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:1383 OnCycleBuildings(NormalizedScreenPosition) — screen->world via screen_position_to_world_position, point query against CurrentBuildingQuadTree, Algo::RemoveIf to drop entries whose BuildablePtr.IsValid() is false, remap through BuildingDataIndexRedirector, take [0], fetch GetInteractWidgetClass(), HUD->RequestWidget(WidgetClass), store in CurrentBuildableUI. Note: despite the 'cycle' name it only ever shows IntersectingBuildings[0]; cycling is unimplemented and a large block of widget Init code is commented out.

CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:441-461 — three blueprint-function hooks (SetOpenMap toggles MapInputContext mapping; SetInventoryVisibility forced to false; UseableBaseWidget) to keep the interact widget from dragging the inventory UI open.

DispatchLifecycleEvent:345-377 — SUBSCRIBE_UOBJECT_METHOD on UFGGameUI::SetShowInventory / SetWindowWantsInventoryAddon whose bodies are ONLY FDebug::DumpStackTraceToLog — pure debug stubs left in, never finished.

Cartograph.Build.cs:39 — enables the EnhancedInput module. AccessTransformers.ini:7-9 — friend access to AFGBuildable, UFGInteractWidget, UFGUserWidget. New assets: IA_CycleBuilding, IMC_UI, BPW_HoverArea, BPW_BuildingUIContainer.
CurrentBuildableUI: UFGInteractWidget* member (header:415) holds the spawned widget with no visible lifecycle/teardown management.
salvageableIdeas: The screen->world->quadtree point-pick in OnCycleBuildings (CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:1383) proves the existing CurrentBuildingQuadTree + BuildingDataIndexRedirector can answer interactive point/region queries cheaply. This is directly reusable: the SAME spatial index should drive localized/partial redraws (issue #10) — query the dirty rect, redraw only buildings in it, instead of full-map redraw on every build event. The branch validates the index is query-ready; the perf fix is to feed build/remove events' bounding boxes into GetElements rather than redrawing everything.

Resolving a map location back to a live AFGBuildable on demand is the right capability — but do it WITHOUT storing a per-building soft pointer. Salvageable version: keep FBuildingData lean and resolve the actor lazily only for the single clicked building (e.g. via the lightweight subsystem index / a sparse side-map keyed by quadtree id), so interaction works with zero per-record memory cost.

Gating an EnhancedInput mapping context on the map open/close (SetOpenMap hook, CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:447) is a clean pattern for adding map-only input without leaking keybinds into normal play — reusable for a future 'trigger full redraw' user command requested in #10.
pitfalls: MEMORY REGRESSION, not a fix: BuildablePtr (TSoftObjectPtr) on every FBuildingData makes the already-criticized memory footprint worse. For the #14 memory goal this branch moves the needle the wrong way. Do not port the field as-is.

Stale/dangling references: TSoftObjectPtr does not auto-clear on actor destruction, and the field is only set in AddExtraData, never updated on remove. The IsValid() filter in OnCycleBuildings papers over this for the click path but the stored paths accumulate; for hot belt placement/removal (the exact #14 trigger) this grows unbounded garbage.

Broken on dedicated servers/clients: BuildablePtr is absent from NetSerialize, so replicated client data has empty pointers and the pick feature does nothing on a joined client — overlaps with the multiplayer fragility in #9.

Unfinished/dead code: SetShowInventory/SetWindowWantsInventoryAddon hooks are stack-trace-dump stubs; the widget Init() path and the actual 'cycle through stacked buildings' logic are commented out; only IntersectingBuildings[0] is ever shown. The 'inventory opening' problem was never solved (commit titled 'Fiddling with inventory opening...').
Per-pixel/per-click DumpStackTraceToLog and several CARTO_LOG calls in the hot UI path would themselves cause hitches if those hooks fire frequently.

Based on a March-2025 pre-1.2 / pre-GameFeature merge-base under Mods/Cartograph/Source/Cartograph; the current branch lives under Mods/GameFeatures/Cartograph and has diverged substantially, so nothing here applies cleanly — it must be re-implemented, not merged.
No widget lifecycle: CurrentBuildableUI is assigned but there's no shown teardown/dedup, risking widget leaks each click.
recommendation: Do NOT merge or cherry-pick this branch for performance/memory work — it is an abandoned UI prototype that, if anything, increases memory use (per-building TSoftObjectPtr) and adds no redraw/data-model optimization. Treat it as archaeology with exactly two takeaways: (1) it confirms CurrentBuildingQuadTree + BuildingDataIndexRedirector can serve fast point/region queries, which is the foundation for the localized partial-redraw fix that issues #10 and #14 actually need; (2) if interactive building pickup is wanted later, resolve the actor lazily for the one clicked building instead of storing a soft pointer on every FBuildingData. The real lag/memory fixes (frame-budgeted localized redraws keyed off build-event bounding boxes, avoiding full-map clears, and trimming FBuildingData size) live in RedrawMap/RedrawMapCoroutine and the data model on the current branch — this branch does not touch any of them.
